hypothesis: Shape-led test: one Tyr anchor plus a Pro-defined bend; reduces flexibility relative to first-round glycine-rich peptides. Cysteine-free, with balanced acidic/basic side chains.
expected_discrimination: Seek simultaneous Y39/S42 contacts across MSA, where their Cα separation is 5.7–5.8 Å, versus 8.4 Å in 8A9L and 7.5 Å in 6CU7; sequence alone does not establish selectivity.

hypothesis: Shape-led test: NPAT turn candidate positions an aromatic anchor and polar arm without a hydrophobic cluster.
expected_discrimination: Target the MSA 40–42 separation of 5.4 Å rather than 6.8/7.1 Å in 8A9L/6CU7; require additional K43/T44 contacts to support the pose.

hypothesis: Shape-led revision of KQYSEGNDTQESK, whose contrast was −1.077: replace EG with PN to test whether reduced linker flexibility improves worst-conformer compatibility.
expected_discrimination: Test a bend spanning Y39–S42, compact in all MSA conformers but wider in both controls; avoid interpreting the original single-conformer contacts as success.

hypothesis: Shape-led test: TPA bend with one Tyr anchor and soluble polar flanks; assess whether modest preorganization avoids assembly clashes.
expected_discrimination: MSA L38–S42 distances are 9.3–9.4 Å, versus 12.2 Å in 8A9L and 4.5 Å in 6CU7, providing opposing geometric mismatches.

hypothesis: Shape-led longer alternative: a localized YPN bend with polar extensions, rather than a uniformly flexible aromatic-acidic linker.
expected_discrimination: Seek the shared MSA L38–G41 span of 9.5–9.8 Å; 6CU7 is sharply folded at 4.4 Å, while rejecting 8A9L additionally requires its wider Y39–S42 geometry.

hypothesis: Charge-led test: a single Asp near a constrained aromatic/polar motif, reducing nonspecific electrostatic attraction relative to multi-acidic designs.
expected_discrimination: K43 alone is insufficient because it is more exposed in 8A9L; require MSA-like Y39–S42 geometry and accessible T44, whose SASA is only 9.0 Å² in 6CU7.

hypothesis: Charge-led matched alternative: substitute a longer Glu side chain for an Asp-type anchor while keeping a compact YPN motif and avoiding net acidic excess.
expected_discrimination: Test K43 anchoring only when coupled to the MSA Y39–S42 separation of 5.7–5.8 Å; both controls have wider separations.

hypothesis: Charge-led test: one localized Asp and one Lys with a Pro/Ala spacer; prioritizes spatially gated K43 recognition over broad acidity.
expected_discrimination: MSA Y39–K43 spans 8.3–8.7 Å versus 9.5 Å in 8A9L and 10.5 Å in 6CU7; side-chain placement must be verified by prediction.

hypothesis: Charge-led revision of KNSYQEGTNDQSKETNQG, the least-negative first-round contrast (−0.722): reduce acidic density and introduce one turn constraint.
expected_discrimination: The parent had only 0.222 contacts/residue in 6XYO; seek improved three-MSA coverage through Y39/S42/K43 anchoring, not merely retained 6XYQ contacts.

hypothesis: Charge-led long alternative: isolated Asp within a mildly basic, polar scaffold; tests whether distributed polar support can replace multiple acidic contacts.
expected_discrimination: Require compact MSA L38–S42 geometry plus T44 engagement; 8A9L is more extended and 6CU7 combines a compressed 38–42 span with poorly exposed T44.

hypothesis: Polar-led test: acid-free Tyr/Ser/Thr/Asn motif to probe hydrogen-bond anchoring without a K43 salt bridge; hydrophobicity is limited to one Tyr.
expected_discrimination: Target joint Y39/S42/T44 recognition; 8A9L has a wider Y39–S42 span, while 6CU7 offers substantially less T44 exposure.

hypothesis: Polar-led revision of QHNSYTGQEDTK: retain His/Tyr but remove both acidic residues and replace the flexible TG segment with a Pro-containing motif.
expected_discrimination: The parent contrast was −2.916 with strong 8A9L contacts; test whether geometry-gated Y39/S42 recognition reduces that bias while avoiding buried G41 in 6CU7.

hypothesis: Polar-led revision of SNYQTNGEQSTDKQ: retain its aromatic/polar character but remove acidic residues and constrain the central linker to address assembly-clash feedback.
expected_discrimination: The parent showed 10.5/9.5 assembly clashes per residue in 6XYP/6XYQ; require low-clash MSA poses and weaker control contacts, exploiting Y39–S42 distance differences.

hypothesis: Polar-led revision of GQNSYTSNQGEDTKNSQ: remove the ED pair and introduce a localized TPA bend to counter the parent's −3.412 contrast.
expected_discrimination: Seek improved worst-MSA contacts without favoring highly exposed 8A9L; require MSA L38–S42 spacing and T44 access absent together in 6CU7.

hypothesis: Polar-led long alternative based on the 22-residue first-round scaffold: retain His/Tyr and polar extensions, remove acidic residues, and add a Pro-defined bend. No cysteine or hydrophobic run.
expected_discrimination: The parent remained weak in 6XYP and clashed with 8A9L; test consistent, low-clash MSA engagement of Y39/S42/T44, with geometric rejection of 8A9L and limited T44 access in 6CU7.

hypothesis: Compact turn variant of RFSPGQDVTRSN, whose minimum MSA contact density was 1.0. Tests R/E46, D/K80 and terminal R/E83 anchoring with limited hydrophobicity.
expected_discrimination: Requires joint E46/80–83 engagement; 8A9L separates E46/K80 by 33.7 Å, while 6CU7 buries E46. Prior motif still favored 6CU7, so selectivity is unproven.

hypothesis: Replace the prior turn glycine with threonine to reduce linker freedom and add a possible Q79/T81 hydrogen-bond contact.
expected_discrimination: Test whether a constrained bridge accommodates MSA E46/K80 distances of 6.8–11.1 Å but loses contacts to separated 8A9L anchors and occluded 6CU7 anchors.

hypothesis: Conservative V-to-I variant of the strongest short first-round motif; tests a slightly larger hydrophobic contact at V82 without a hydrophobic run.
expected_discrimination: V82 is exposed in all MSA structures (80.6–119.7 Å²), less exposed in 6CU7 (35.1 Å²); E46 co-engagement is needed to discriminate 8A9L.

hypothesis: F-to-Y substitution preserves the compact turn while testing an additional polar contact near Q79/T81.
expected_discrimination: Combined E46 and Q79/T81 anchoring could penalize distant 8A9L geometry and buried Q79/T81 in 6CU7; local polar binding alone may not discriminate.

hypothesis: Extend the promising short motif with a polar, proline-ended tail to test support near E83/G84 without a long flexible GS linker.
expected_discrimination: Seek retained contacts across all MSA conformers without the 6CU7 contact enrichment seen previously; G84 proximity alone is insufficient for selectivity.

hypothesis: Remove the second basic anchor and introduce an acidic terminus, testing E46/K80 recognition rather than nonspecific attraction to exposed E83.
expected_discrimination: May reduce attraction to control E83, especially highly exposed E83 in 8A9L; MSA compatibility must survive the loss of an E83 salt bridge.

hypothesis: Charge-balanced derivative of RFSPGQDVTRSN; retains the E46-directed basic group and K80-directed acid while replacing the E83-directed arginine.
expected_discrimination: Tests whether lower basicity reduces the original motif's 6CU7 preference; discrimination still requires accessible E46 plus K80 rather than K80 alone.

hypothesis: D-to-E substitution tests longer acidic-side-chain reach toward K80 across the three MSA geometries.
expected_discrimination: Could tolerate MSA E46/K80 variation while requiring both anchors; 8A9L separates them, and 6CU7 exposes little E46 despite similar geometry.

hypothesis: Replace both arginines with histidines to test weaker, pH-dependent acidic-residue anchoring and reduce constitutive positive charge.
expected_discrimination: Potentially reduces control binding driven by exposed glutamates; retain only if all MSA poses engage E46 and K80. Test pH dependence explicitly.

hypothesis: Alternative lysine-based, turn-constrained charge arrangement tests E46/K80/E83 anchoring without reproducing the GS-rich first-round designs.
expected_discrimination: A compact multi-anchor pose could reject 8A9L's distant E46 and 6CU7's occluded V48/Q79; lysine substitutions are exploratory, not predicted improvements.

hypothesis: Polar turn scaffold adds T/N contacts around Q79/T81 while retaining one aromatic group and spaced charged anchors.
expected_discrimination: Seek simultaneous E46 and Q79/T81 contacts: these are accessible in MSA, separated in 8A9L and largely buried in 6CU7. Prior NPG variants lacked selectivity.

hypothesis: Replace a flexible segment of the first-round long turn motif with T/P; test reduced conformational freedom while preserving polar flanks.
expected_discrimination: Constrain bridging within MSA E46/E83 distances of 14.7–20.6 Å rather than 42.8 Å in 8A9L; require no assembly clashes in 6XYO and exclusion of buried 6CU7 anchors.

hypothesis: Short helix-biased alternative places polar and charged groups on a less flexible scaffold; tests E46/K80/E83 contacts without a glycine-rich linker.
expected_discrimination: Compact presentation may favor MSA anchor proximity over 8A9L separation; 6CU7 rejection must come from accessibility, since its distances resemble 6XYO.

hypothesis: Extend the helix-biased alternative with a soluble polar tail to accommodate MSA distance variation and contact Q79/T81.
expected_discrimination: Tests geometry plus accessibility rather than sequence recognition: all receptors share the anchors, but 6CU7 buries Q79/T81 and 8A9L separates E46 from them.

hypothesis: Long, predominantly polar alternative with one proline hinge and balanced side-chain charge; avoids the repeated GS linker of the least-negative first-round design.
expected_discrimination: Could span MSA E46/E83 distances of 14.7–20.6 Å while requiring V48/Q79 access absent in 6CU7; check that flexibility does not permit 8A9L binding or reproduce prior 6XYO assembly clashes.

hypothesis: 10-aa polar-anchor hypothesis: Tyr/Leu provide limited V66 packing; Thr/Ser target T64 without requiring buried N65. Removes bulky Trp from poorly discriminating round-one motifs.
expected_discrimination: Test higher compatibility across MSA, where T64/V66 are more exposed, than BOTH controls; SASA layer-count differences make this provisional.

hypothesis: 11-aa shape hypothesis: SPG biases a bend, with Tyr/Leu bracketing a small polar surface near T64/V66/G67.
expected_discrimination: Test adaptation to MSA V66–G68 spacing of 5.5 Å versus 5.2 Å in 8A9L and 5.9 Å in 6CU7; differences are small.

hypothesis: 12-aa shape/polar hypothesis: retain TPG but replace Trp with Phe and limit hydrophobic density. Round-one TPG-containing peptides did not achieve positive contrast.
expected_discrimination: Seek a constrained T64/V66-facing pose across MSA rather than the broader control contacts observed previously; weaker binding to each control must be verified.

hypothesis: 12-aa flexible polar-anchor hypothesis: NAG replaces a proline turn, permitting accommodation of all three MSA geometries without demanding N65 side-chain access.
expected_discrimination: Test recognition of exposed T64/V66 plus moderately accessible G67; 6CU7 is less accessible, while discrimination from 8A9L must arise from pose geometry.

hypothesis: 13-aa shape hypothesis: SPA reduces glycine flexibility relative to SPG; separated Tyr/Leu anchors avoid an extended hydrophobic run.
expected_discrimination: Test the MSA V63–V70 span of 7.7–8.1 Å against 8.6 Å in 8A9L and 8.3 Å in 6CU7, without assuming direct V63 binding.

hypothesis: 13-aa polar-anchor hypothesis: Ser/Thr/Gln support T64 recognition, with Tyr/Leu as modest V66 anchors and balanced charged termini.
expected_discrimination: Prioritize T64/V66 over N65, whose SASA varies strongly among MSA conformers; require lower predicted compatibility with both controls despite similar local backbone geometry.

hypothesis: 14-aa acidic-solubility hypothesis: retain YTPG from round-one EEQYTPGNFQSTEE but replace Phe with Leu and reduce reliance on Asn anchoring. Parent minimum-MSA contact density was 0.143 versus maximum-control 3.5.
expected_discrimination: Test whether reduced aromatic surface reverses control-biased contacts while maintaining T64/V66 anchoring; acidic residues are solvent-facing, not proposed patch salt bridges.

hypothesis: 14-aa balanced-charge shape hypothesis: Phe/Leu flank a TPGTS bend, while terminal Lys/Glu/Asp improve solubility without assigning unsupported electrostatic contacts.
expected_discrimination: Seek MSA-compatible V66–G68 geometry at 5.5 Å and penalize both the shorter 8A9L and longer 6CU7 spacing; prediction is speculative.

hypothesis: 14-aa low-aromatic alternative: His/Leu replace the Trp/Phe pair, reducing nonspecific hydrophobic capture while preserving a polar turn.
expected_discrimination: Test whether T64-directed polar contacts survive in all MSA structures while control contact density falls; His introduces an experimentally testable pH dependence.

hypothesis: 16-aa shape hypothesis: SAP provides a less flexible bend than glycine-rich motifs, with only two separated hydrophobic anchors.
expected_discrimination: Test a compact pose around T64/V66/G67 that fits all MSA structures but not BOTH controls; avoid dependence on the more buried G68/A69.

hypothesis: 17-aa polar-scaffold hypothesis: extend a small Tyr/Leu recognition core with soluble polar flanks rather than adding aromatic anchors. Round-one longer scaffolds still favored controls.
expected_discrimination: Evaluate whether flanks remain solvent-exposed while the core recognizes MSA T64/V66 accessibility; reject poses gaining contacts through exposed control V70.

hypothesis: 16-aa reversed-anchor hypothesis: reverse Leu/Tyr order around QPGT to sample a different binding orientation from round-one aromatic motifs.
expected_discrimination: Test simultaneous accommodation of the MSA T64–V66 distance of 6.7–6.9 Å and V66–G68 distance of 5.5 Å; both controls must score worse.

hypothesis: 18-aa shape/charge hypothesis: APG introduces a localized bend; acidic/polar flanks discourage broad hydrophobic surface association.
expected_discrimination: Seek a geometry-selective T64/V66 pose rather than generic exposed-patch binding, particularly to 8A9L; 6CU7 discrimination may additionally reflect lower accessibility.

hypothesis: 20-aa flexible-scaffold alternative: retain polar-rich chemistry but use Tyr/Leu instead of Trp/Phe and omit proline to test whether imposed turns caused MSA incompatibility.
expected_discrimination: All round-one contrasts were negative; test improved minimum-MSA versus maximum-control contact density while requiring compatibility with each MSA and reduced compatibility with each control.

hypothesis: 23-aa extended shape hypothesis: a compact YQAPGTQL core supplies restrained hydrophobic anchoring; balanced, polar flanks probe soluble presentation. All candidates are cysteine-free linear peptides.
expected_discrimination: Test whether a localized core exploits MSA V66–G68 geometry and T64 exposure without recruiting control V63/V70 surfaces; longer flanks must not create nonspecific control contacts.

hypothesis: 11 aa; compact shape anchor. Replace the Tyr in SVQYNGQTVS with Phe and introduce a GP turn to test packing against V48/V49/V52 beside H50; charged termini support solubility.
expected_discrimination: Test compact MSA packing rather than generic exposure: 48–76 is 5.3–9.8 Å in MSA versus 30.4 Å in 8A9L. 6CU7 buries V48/V49/V52. Parent contrast was unfavorable (-2.4).

hypothesis: 11 aa; Leu/Tyr anchor with a PG turn and polar flanks. Targets the conserved 48–52 contour without requiring exposed A53, A76 or A78.
expected_discrimination: A compact pose could favor MSA over the separated 48–76 surfaces in 8A9L; 6CU7 occludes the local anchor. Local backbone similarity alone cannot establish selectivity.

hypothesis: 12 aa; separated Phe/Val packing elements and a constrained GP bend test a less flexible alternative to first-round glycine-rich peptides.
expected_discrimination: Seek contacts with accessible MSA V48/V49/H50/V52 without the assembly clashes seen previously. 8A9L lacks the nearby 76 surface; 6CU7 buries the valines.

hypothesis: 12 aa; a single Pro adjacent to Tyr tests a shallow bent interface around H50/G51, retaining soluble polar flanks rather than adding a long hydrophobic segment.
expected_discrimination: ESVYNGSTVQGSK favored 8A9L in round one (contrast -4.077); the Pro substitution tests shape restriction. MSA compaction and 6CU7 burial are hypotheses, not demonstrated advantages.

hypothesis: 14 aa; compact Leu/Tyr/Val core with charged extensions. Tests whether reduced core flexibility improves cross-MSA placement while extensions remain solvent-facing.
expected_discrimination: Require compatibility despite A53 SASA changing from 17.2 to 81.1–83.6 Å across MSA. Compact 48–76 geometry distinguishes 8A9L; buried 48–52 distinguishes 6CU7.

hypothesis: 10 aa; balanced-charge polar anchor. Asp/Tyr offers alternative hydrogen-bonding and aromatic interactions with exposed H50, while Pro constrains the local contour.
expected_discrimination: H50 is more exposed in 8A9L than MSA, so H50 binding alone is insufficient; test a geometry-dependent multi-contact pose. H50 exposure is much lower in 6CU7 (14.7 Å²).

hypothesis: 11 aa; Phe plus an His/Asp polar module tests pH-sensitive recognition of H50 with small residues accommodating G51. No target salt bridge is assumed.
expected_discrimination: Compare pH-dependent poses across all five structures: MSA H50 SASA is 86.4–92.4 Å² versus 158.1 in 8A9L and 14.7 in 6CU7. Selectivity must additionally depend on MSA packing.

hypothesis: 12 aa; Tyr/Asp/Gln anchoring with no glycine tests a less floppy polar scaffold. Modest net negative charge and isolated Val limit hydrophobic aggregation risk.
expected_discrimination: EVQYDSQTVK gave contrast -4.0; altered spacing tests that failure rather than assuming acidic anchoring works. Seek compact MSA contacts absent in 8A9L and inaccessible in 6CU7.

hypothesis: 12 aa; one Trp probes stronger aromatic contact with H50/V49, while Asp, Asn and Thr provide polar compensation. Avoids a continuous hydrophobic run.
expected_discrimination: Trp may also favor exposed 8A9L; retain only poses exploiting compact MSA topology. 6CU7 occludes V49 and most of the surrounding patch.

hypothesis: 14 aa; His/Asp and Tyr provide complementary polar/aromatic anchoring, with Pro testing a bent scaffold. Avoids dependence on variable A76/A78 exposure.
expected_discrimination: Test recognition of accessible MSA 48–52 plus its compact surroundings, not sequence identity. 8A9L separates 48 from 76 by 30.4 Å; 6CU7 buries 48–52.

hypothesis: 12 aa; alternative Trp/Val shape anchor with a PG turn. Builds on NQSYVTGQSN, whose MSA contacts were relatively consistent (0.5–0.7 per residue), but changes its flexible core.
expected_discrimination: Parent contrast was -2.1, so this tests—not predicts—improvement against exposed 8A9L. Compact MSA geometry and inaccessible 6CU7 anchors provide the proposed filters.

hypothesis: 14 aa; Leu substitution and Pro restriction retain the polar SQNY motif. Tests recovery of cross-MSA contacts rather than merely lowering control contacts.
expected_discrimination: SQNYVSGTQNSK had low 8A9L contacts but near-zero 6XYP/6XYQ contacts. Require improved worst-MSA contact density while preserving weaker compatibility with buried 6CU7 and separated 8A9L.

hypothesis: 16 aa; a compact Trp/Leu anchor embedded in a soluble polar scaffold. A GP turn tests whether longer peptides can avoid the extensive assembly clashes of round one.
expected_discrimination: Evaluate full assemblies: MSA A76/A78 are exposed in 6XYO but nearly buried in 6XYP/6XYQ, so they must remain optional contacts. 8A9L separation and 6CU7 burial are negative-selection features.

hypothesis: 18 aa; distributed Tyr/Leu/Val anchors and a single Pro allow peripheral adjustment while maintaining a constrained central contact near H50/G51.
expected_discrimination: ESQNYVGTNSQTVQSK retained contacts across MSA but had contrast -2.438. Test whether core restriction reduces 8A9L preference without demanding buried A76/A78 contacts in 6XYP/6XYQ; 6CU7 remains occluded.

hypothesis: 24 aa; long polar-tail alternative with a localized Phe/Leu turn-containing core. Tests whether nonbinding extensions can improve solubility without disrupting compact 48–52 anchoring.
expected_discrimination: The previous 22-aa peptide lost 6XYO contacts and had 11.182 assembly clashes per residue there. Require clash-free compatibility across MSA, weaker 8A9L binding despite its exposure, and exclusion from buried 6CU7.
